issues.legal_issue: Property inherited by a Hindu male from his maternal grandfather is not ancestral property in his hands in relation to his sons under Punjab customary law.
material_facts: The father and son were governed by Punjab customary law.
The father inherited the disputed property from his maternal grandfather.
The son sought to challenge the father's mortgage and sale of the property as alienations of ancestral property.
issues.conclusion: The property was not ancestral property in relation to the son, who therefore had no right to bring the suit challenging the alienations.
issues.legal_principle: Under Punjab customary law, ancestral property, as regards sons, is property inherited from a direct male lineal ancestor. The Court approved Narotam Chand v. Mst. Durga Devi and relied on Rattigan's Digest, paragraph 59, and the reasoning in Attar Singh v. Thakar Singh and Muhammad Husain Khan v. Babu Kishva Nandan Sahai. It did not approve Lehna v. Musammat Thakri or Musammat Attar Kaur v. Nikkoo. The Court noted that, under Hindu law, property inherited from a maternal grandfather is likewise not ancestral property in relation to a son.

predicates.customary_law_inheritance_case: The proceeding concerns whether inherited property is ancestral under the customary law governing the family.
predicates.father_inherited_from_maternal_grandfath: A father inherited the property from his maternal grandfather.
predicates.claimant_is_his_son: The person claiming an interest in the property is the father's son.

issues.definition: When a customary-law inheritance case concerns property inherited by a father from his maternal grandfather and a claimant who is his son, the property is not ancestral in relation to that son.

issues.legal_issue: The rule of stare decisis does not prevent departure from an erroneous decision where it has not been consistently followed and reversal will not disturb titles, contracts, or the general course of dealing.
material_facts: The appeal challenged earlier decisions that treated property inherited through a maternal grandfather as ancestral under Punjab customary law.
The earlier Full Bench decision had not been based on proof of the alleged custom, had been challenged in later proceedings, and had been reversed by a later Full Bench.
The Privy Council had made observations that impaired the earlier decision's validity.

The Court considered that reversal would not disturb any title or contract or alter the general course of dealing; the right conferred by the earlier decision was only an option to challenge an alienation.
The Court found the earlier decision unsustainable as a decision on the relevant custom.
issues.conclusion: The doctrine of stare decisis did not bar the Court from holding that the earlier decisions were incorrectly decided.
issues.legal_principle: Stare decisis is based on expediency and public policy but is not inflexible; prior decisions need not be followed where they are erroneous and doing so would perpetuate error. The Court relied on the formulations in Halsbury's Laws of England and Corpus Juris Secundum, and considered the history of Lehna v. Musammat Thakri, Musammat Attar Kaur v. Nikkoo, Attar Singh v. Thakar Singh, Muhammad Husain Khan v. Babu Kishva Nandan Sahai, and Narotam Chand v. Mst. Durga Devi.

rule.if: precedent_review_appeal and earlier_rule_found_erroneous and earlier_rule_not_consistently_followed and reversal_will_not_disturb_titles_contracts_or_general_dealings

predicates.precedent_review_appeal: The proceeding asks a reviewing court to decide whether to depart from an earlier judicial rule.
predicates.earlier_rule_found_erroneous: The court finds that the earlier rule is unsupported or incorrect on the issue being decided.
predicates.earlier_rule_not_consistently_followed: The earlier rule has been challenged or departed from rather than consistently followed over time.
predicates.reversal_will_not_disturb_titles_contrac: The court finds that reversing the earlier rule will not disturb titles or contracts or alter the general course of dealing.

issues.definition: In an appeal reviewing precedent, stare decisis does not bar departure when the earlier rule is found erroneous, has not been consistently followed, and reversal will not disturb titles, contracts, or general dealings.
